quests.instruction: You swing across the monkey bars. Which parts of your hands curl around each rung?
quests.hint: They bend to hook over the bar.
quests.explanation: Fingers curl around the rung and hold on, while your arms and shoulders pull you forward.
quests.funFact: Hanging and swinging builds strength in the muscles of your hands and forearms.

quests.instruction: You are on a swing and want to stop. Which body parts do you drag along the ground to slow down?
quests.hint: They touch the ground before the rest of you does.
quests.explanation: Dragging your feet on the ground creates friction, which slows the swing.
quests.funFact: A swing takes about the same time to go back and forth whether you swing low or high.

quests.instruction: You hang upside down from a bar, hooked by the bend behind which joints?
quests.hint: The hollow behind them is just right for hooking over a bar.
quests.explanation: The bend behind the knee fits over a bar, and your leg muscles hold you there.
quests.funFact: When you hang upside down, extra blood flows to your head, so your face may turn red.

quests.instruction: You stand on one leg and lift the other knee to slide on a sock. Which joint at the top of your leg bends to lift it?
quests.hint: It lets your thigh swing up toward your chest.
quests.explanation: The hip bends to bring your thigh forward and up, so you can reach your foot.
quests.funFact: Standing on one leg to get dressed is good balance practice.

quests.instruction: Make a fist. Which round bumps pop up on the back of your hand?
quests.hint: They are where your fingers join your hand.
quests.explanation: Knuckles are the joints at the base of your fingers, and they stick out when you curl your fingers into a fist.
quests.funFact: The bumps you see are the rounded ends of the long bones in your palm.

quests.instruction: You wring out a wet towel by twisting your hands in opposite directions. Which part of your arms does most of the twisting work?
quests.hint: It is between your elbow and your wrist.
quests.explanation: The twist of your hand comes from the forearm, where one bone rolls over the other.
quests.funFact: The two bones in your forearm cross over each other when you turn your palm down.

quests.instruction: In a tug of war, you lean back and dig which parts of your feet into the ground to grip it?
quests.hint: They are at the back of your feet.
quests.explanation: Digging in your heels gives you grip, and leaning back lets your body weight help pull the rope.
quests.funFact: Tug of war teams often put their heaviest player at the back, and that player is called the anchor.

quests.instruction: Without saying a word, you show surprise by lifting which part of your face?
quests.hint: They sit above your eyes.
quests.explanation: Raising your eyebrows widens your eyes and shows surprise or curiosity.
quests.funFact: In many places, a quick eyebrow raise is a friendly hello signal.

quests.instruction: When you smile big, which soft parts of your face get lifted up?
quests.hint: They bulge up when you grin.
quests.explanation: Muscles in your face pull your cheeks up and out when you smile.
quests.funFact: A real, happy smile also crinkles the corners of the eyes.

quests.instruction: You stare down at a tablet for a long time. Which part gets tired from holding your head tipped forward?
quests.hint: The muscles along the back of it do the holding.
quests.explanation: The more your head tips forward, the harder your neck muscles work to hold it up.
quests.funFact: Holding a screen higher, at eye level, lets your neck relax.

quests.instruction: A hiking backpack has a wide belt that buckles around which part of your body to share the weight?
quests.hint: It rests on strong bones at the sides of your body.
quests.explanation: A hip belt moves weight off your shoulders and onto your hips, which have strong bones and big muscles.
quests.funFact: A well-fitted pack carries much of its weight on the hips instead of the shoulders.

quests.instruction: You read a story in a dim room. Which body parts get tired from working harder?
quests.hint: They need good light to see small letters easily.
quests.explanation: Dim light makes your eyes work harder to see small print, so they can feel tired.
quests.funFact: Reading in dim light does not damage your eyes for good, but it can make them tired.

quests.instruction: Before you dive under the water, you take a big breath. Which parts of your body fill with that air?
quests.hint: They are inside your chest.
quests.explanation: Air travels down your windpipe into your lungs, which hold it while you swim underwater.
quests.funFact: Your lungs are filled with millions of tiny air sacs.

quests.instruction: After a long bath, which parts of your hands get wrinkly like a prune?
quests.hint: They are at the very ends of your fingers.
quests.explanation: Your fingertips wrinkle when they stay wet for a while.
quests.funFact: The wrinkles may help you grip wet things, a bit like tiny treads on a tire.

quests.instruction: To glide through the water like a dolphin, swimmers point which parts of their feet straight behind them?
quests.hint: They are at the very tips of your feet.
quests.explanation: Pointing your toes makes your legs and feet long and smooth, so they cut through the water.
quests.funFact: A swimmer who stretches the arms overhead and points the toes pushes off a pool wall like a rocket.

quests.instruction: To do a shimmy, you shake which parts of your body quickly forward and back?
quests.hint: You also lift them when you shrug.
quests.explanation: Shoulders can roll, shrug, and shake, so they are easy to move to music.
quests.funFact: The shimmy has been a popular dance move for more than a hundred years.

quests.instruction: Tap dancers wear shoes with small metal plates so that which body parts make rhythm on the floor?
quests.hint: They hit the floor with every step.
quests.explanation: Metal plates on the bottoms of the shoes make a clicking sound each time the feet touch the floor.
quests.funFact: A skilled tap dancer can make several sounds in a single second.

quests.instruction: To wink at a friend, you close just one of which parts?
quests.hint: They cover your eyes when you blink.
quests.explanation: A wink closes one eyelid on purpose, while a blink closes both without you thinking.
quests.funFact: Some people find winking hard because the muscles of the two eyes like to work together.

quests.instruction: You roll a ball of play dough into a long snake between the flat parts of your hands. Which parts do the rolling?
quests.hint: They are the broad, padded parts of your hands.
quests.explanation: The palms press and roll the dough evenly, while your fingers stay out of the way.
quests.funFact: Playing with dough helps build strength and control in the hands.

quests.instruction: You sip juice through a straw. Which parts close tightly around it?
quests.hint: They make a seal.
quests.explanation: Your lips close around the straw so that no air leaks in.
quests.funFact: A straw works because the air outside pushes the drink up when you lower the pressure in your mouth.

quests.instruction: A recorder has small holes along the top. Which parts of your hands cover them to change the note?
quests.hint: You can lift them one at a time.
quests.explanation: Covering different holes changes how the air moves through the recorder, so you hear different notes.
quests.funFact: Covering more holes makes the note lower.

quests.instruction: You race around the playground and feel something pounding in your chest. Which part is working faster?
quests.hint: You can feel it when you press your hand on your chest.
quests.explanation: Your heart beats faster during exercise, so your muscles get more of the blood they need.
quests.funFact: A child's heart can beat more than twice as fast during hard exercise as it does at rest.

quests.instruction: At night, a muscle at the back of your lower leg suddenly squeezes tight and hurts. Which part is it?
quests.hint: It is on the back of your leg, below the knee.
quests.explanation: A cramp is a muscle tightening suddenly. Gently stretching and walking around helps it relax.
quests.funFact: Cramps are common, and drinking water and gentle stretching can help.

quests.instruction: After running a lot in new shoes, the front of your lower legs feels sore. Which part is that?
quests.hint: Soccer players wear guards over them.
quests.explanation: Shins can get sore when you do a lot of running, especially on hard ground. Resting and building up slowly helps.
quests.funFact: Good shoes and softer ground can make running easier on your lower legs.

quests.instruction: Your arm has three big joints: the shoulder, the elbow, and one more near your hand. Which is it?
quests.hint: You turn your hand with it when you wave.
quests.explanation: The shoulder, elbow, and wrist are the three main joints of the arm, working together like a chain.
quests.funFact: Your hand can reach almost any spot because each joint in the chain adds a little movement.

quests.instruction: In many places, people carry heavy loads on top of which part of their body?
quests.hint: It sits above the neck.
quests.explanation: Carrying a load on the head works because the spine can balance it when you stand straight.
quests.funFact: People who carry loads this way learn to walk with a very straight back and a steady head.

quests.instruction: Skates have stiff boots to support which joints just above the feet?
quests.hint: They connect the feet to the legs.
quests.explanation: The boot holds the ankles steady, so they do not wobble sideways.
quests.funFact: Skating improves balance because your body makes tiny corrections all the time.

quests.instruction: When you first learn to ride a bike, it feels hard, but with practice it gets easier. Which part learns the pattern so it feels natural?
quests.hint: It controls all of your movements.
quests.explanation: With practice, your brain strengthens the connections that control a skill, so it starts to feel automatic.
quests.funFact: Once you learn to ride a bike, you usually do not forget how.

quests.instruction: You lift a book with your arm bent. Which part of your arm swings upward around the elbow like a lever?
quests.hint: It is the part that ends at your wrist.
quests.explanation: The forearm swings around the elbow like a lever and lifts the book.
quests.funFact: The farther a load is from the elbow, the harder the muscles must work to lift it.

quests.instruction: You lie face down and lift your arms and legs off the floor. Which part of your body does most of that work?
quests.hint: It is the side of your body that faces the ceiling.
quests.explanation: Lifting your arms and legs from the floor uses the muscles of your back, which also keep you standing tall.
quests.funFact: Your back muscles work quietly all day to hold your spine upright.
